newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end flat to lower, eye U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end flat to lower, eye U.S. rates.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to lower Friday as thin activity kept the market within ranges before a clearer direction is staked out next week when the U.S. Federal Reserve gives word on monetary policy.
"It is confusing to know" what the Federal Reserve will do with rates, meaning players "want to be flat" ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committe meeting, said a trader.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 92-3/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was down $0.10 at 115.05.

Another trader said most players in Buenos Aires are expecting a 25 basis point rise in the Fed funds rate, in which case the market will probably fall before springing back up a couple of sessions later.
"The market is fundamentally firm," said the first trader.
However, conflicting indicators on the U.S. economy have led to uncertainty. For instance if the Federal Reserve were to hike rates by 50 basis points, there could be a bigger sell-off.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.93 percent from 6.63 percent.
